stem.text: In 1865 Kekulé suggested a ring structure for benzene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$, in which a hydrogen atom is attached to each carbon atom.

stem.alt: Kekulé structure of benzene: six-membered carbon ring with alternating double bonds, one hydrogen on each carbon
stem.label: Kekulé structure

stem.text: In this structure all of the bonds remain in the places shown. Assuming this is the structure of benzene, how many isomers of dichlorobenzene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$, would exist?
